text:
jen: Heads-up — multiple CI deploys just failed in prod and staging with 401/403s. Started ~10:15am UTC, looks correlated with the runner pool scale-up.

sam: Saw that. Error from deploy logs: `error: token_expired_or_invalid` then `insufficient_scope` on retry.

maria: Do we have a recent change to token TTL or audience? I remember a policy landed that prunes ephemeral tokens under heavy load.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] job 4821 failed: http 403 (token: service-ci-runner@infra).

jen: We rotated the CI service account policy yesterday to enforce max lifetime 15m (security request). Runners usually request ephemeral creds with a 20m window.

sam: That mismatch would explain it. But why intermittent? Some jobs succeed, some fail immediately.

maria: My hypothesis: deploy job requests token -> CI proxy mints short TTL (15m) -> high concurrency causes reuse of cached token for subsequent jobs but with truncated expiry, so token is already expiring when the runner uses it. Repro steps locally: 1) request token; 2) sleep 14m 30s; 3) attempt long job -> 401.

alex: Quick log snippet from runner: ```
[2026-03-17T10:16:22Z] token_expiry: 2026-03-17T10:31:45Z
[2026-03-17T10:16:24Z] request_start
[2026-03-17T10:31:50Z] http 401 unauthorized
```

liz: Could also be clock skew between runners and token issuer. What is NTP status on the autoscaled runners?

jen: NTP looks fine in a sample. I think it's TTL trimming + token cache race. We have a cache layer in the CI proxy that tries to dedupe mint requests and serve a single token to many runners; if the first request gets a 15m token, subsequent rapid requests get the same token but with an effective shorter life due to propagation delays.

security: This is a security policy by design (limit long-lived credentials). We can issue exceptions but would prefer a safe workaround.

sam: Short-term mitigation: disable cache dedupe for token mint in the CI proxy (costly) or bump policy to 20m for the CI service account. Long-term: make proxy return tokens with a small buffer (e.g., mint for 16m and set TTL claim to 15m) or implement per-request TTL negotiation.

maria: Another immediate workaround: have the deploy job perform a fresh token fetch immediately before the critical deploy step instead of relying on the cached token from job start. Add `IMMEDIATE_TOKEN_REFRESH=true` env for the deploy pipeline.

jen: Can we do a quick test in staging? I can patch the proxy to disable dedupe for 1 hour. Who can own the rollback if something breaks?

alex: I can deploy the proxy change to staging in 5. Will run 50 parallel deploys to check.

liz: Also notify on-call infra so we can revert. @oncall-infra FYI — expect a brief config change test for token handling in staging.

ops-bot: @oncall-infra pager triggered for proxy staging deploy (change set: token-cache-dedupe=false).

jen: If staging looks good, we either 1) temporarily relax lifetime for CI SA to 20m and schedule a follow-up design for token buffer, or 2) keep lifetime but require per-job refresh and adjust runners. Which is lower risk?

security: Option 1 is acceptable for <48h if logged and approved by Security. I will open an exception ticket.

sam: I'll coordinate the staging test and collect success/fail counts. If we see >99% success under concurrency, we'll escalate to prod change with rollback plan.

maria: Note for support notes: root cause = policy TTL (15m) + proxy-caching dedupe + high concurrency causing effective expiry window. Workarounds: per-job refresh OR temporarily increase SA TTL OR disable cache dedupe.

jen: Thanks — adding reproduction steps and patch plan to the support ticket.

alex: Staging run started. Will post results in ~10m.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] staging-run-130: 50 parallel deploys started.

alex: Staging results: 50/50 success after disabling cache dedupe. No 401/403s.

jen: Ok let's proceed with security exception and a small prod rollout of proxy change behind a canary. Keep monitoring token error rate.

security: Exception ticket opened: SEC-2026-321. Approver: @security-lead. Logged TTL bump to 20m for `service-ci-runner@infra` while we implement safer buffer logic.

sam: Created follow-up engineering task to implement token-buffering and per-request TTL negotiation: ENG-5123.

maria: I'll draft a postmortem note for the incident channel explaining tradeoffs and action items.

jen: Great. Closing this thread for the immediate outage; will update with PROD canary status. :thumbsup:
